title: Choose the visual world
question: Third hand, steered to layered depth, clear text and timeline visualizations. The roll assigned Survey sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Survey sheet
options.lineage: USGS topographic quadrangles of the Cascades, read as a night-relief sheet
options.thesis: The site is a survey sheet: a deep spruce ground carrying stacked grid and contour layers, with content on raised plates and experience drawn as an elevation profile.
options.viewport: Nav on a plate over the sheet; the name and intro on the highest plate; links as a map legend; below, experience as a trail profile where each role is a waypoint and the current one is the summit in the route colour.
options.risk: The map layers must stay quiet; if contours thicken, the sheet turns into wallpaper behind the text.

raised.raise: Elevation is rank: the plate that matters most sits highest, with the longest, softest shadow; nothing else signals importance.
The ground is committed to one hue, deep spruce, never a neutral grey, so the page is never dim or flat.
Past stays visible: earlier roles remain on the profile as fainter traces rather than disappearing.
Sections are separated by ground showing through between plates, not by divider rules.
Motion moves in whole grid steps: plates settle onto the grid rather than drifting.

options.label: Layered architecture stack
options.thesis: The profile as an exploded stack of translucent planes, each a layer of who you are, labelled by leaders on a flat grid beside it.
materials: isometric planes on a shared grid
options.viewport: An isometric stack of four planes (Education, Work, Leadership, Interests) at right; name, intro and links at left; hovering a label lifts its plane.
options.risk: Isometric stacks are common on tech landing pages; familiar, and the planes can't hold much text.

options.label: Demoscene depth field
options.thesis: Rank is depth: the front line of text holds still and bright while sparse star layers drift behind at slower speeds; nothing is boxed.
options.viewport: Name and intro on the front plane; experience lines sit one depth back, dimmer and wider-spaced; one amber caret marks the active route.
options.case: Programmers love the demoscene (beats the survey on identification); no rules or boxes makes long pages harder to scan.
options.risk: Black void is darker than you asked for; drifting layers must stop for reading.

options.label: Quarterly on a lit desk
options.thesis: Cream leaves on an oltremare ground under raking light.
options.viewport: Leaves floating on a blue desk with a giant vermilion numeral.
options.case: Bembo-only serif and cream leaves break the sans and dark pins.

options.label: Seedbed lobes
options.thesis: Floating white capsules over a saturated green field.
options.viewport: Green field, capsule nav, oversized headline.
options.case: Bright ground and many accents break dark and constrained.

options.label: Orizuru crane sequence
options.thesis: Vermilion washi folded in thirty-two steps.
options.viewport: A red sheet with numbered fold steps.
options.case: Red ground and a fold metaphor with nothing to fold.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.thesis: Blocks cut from cumulus with sky-blue voids.
options.viewport: White cloud blocks with blue gaps.
options.case: White ground and volumetric spectacle; no link to the subject.

options.label: Depot destination blind
options.thesis: Green cloth courses stepping under one window.
options.viewport: A rolling blind of caps legends.
options.case: One-size caps kills reading hierarchy for articles.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer portfolio: centred column, name, bio, icon links, experience list.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line role, short bio, a row of icon links, then experience entries in soft cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other developer sites by design.
